subject: mathematics
question_text: If a = i − j − k and b = 2i − 3j + k, then find the projection VECTOR of b on a.

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Junior Inter Maths-1A (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.104 — from the book's separate "STAR QUESTIONS PLUS" bank, answer 156. That bank (book pp.98-111, answers 142-180) sits AFTER all the numbered chapters and is organised by chapter rather than forming part of any chapter's own inventory; it is authored into this unit because that is where the question belongs on the paper (founder decision 2026-08-22). SECTION: classed VSAQ on its length and shape. The bank prints no mark cut, so this classification is OURS. Printed appearances: AP 17. The projection VECTOR, not the projection length. The length is (a·b)/|a|; the vector keeps the direction of a, so it divides by |a|² and multiplies by a itself. ⚠ THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S — the bank prints no [N Marks] tags anywhere. The shapes used follow the splits the book DOES print elsewhere: 1+1 for a 2-mark VSAQ (answers 100, 101 on book p.82), 1+1+1+1 or 1+2+1 for a 4-mark SAQ (answers 58, 59 on p.63 and 61 on p.64), and the granular split for a 7-mark LAQ (answer 32 on p.44). This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — name each move in order.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Find a·b and |a|
steps.margin_note: First mark. Two ingredients: the dot product on top, and the SQUARE of the length of a underneath.
steps.memory_tip: Two ingredients: the dot product on top, and the SQUARE of |a| underneath.

accept: the dot product is four and the length of a squared is three
a dot b comes to four and mod a is root three
find the dot product and the square of the length
a dot b four, mod a square three

steps.why: It is |a|², not |a|, that goes underneath — because one factor of |a| turns a into a unit vector and the other scales the projection.

steps.label: Apply the projection formula
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Projection vector of b on a = (a·b / |a|²) a. The direction is a, so a stays in the answer.
steps.memory_tip: (a·b / |a|²)a — the direction is a, so a stays in the answer.
lines: Projection vector of b on a = (a·b / |a|²) a

recall.must_convey: That the projection vector is (a·b/|a|²)a = (4/3)(i − j − k).
accept: the projection vector is four thirds times i minus j minus k
multiply the scalar four over three by the vector a
the answer keeps the direction of a
four by three into a vector
projection vector is four thirds of a

steps.why: A projection VECTOR must be a vector, so a has to appear in the answer. A bare number would be the projection length instead.
common_mistakes: Stopping at 4/√3 and calling it the projection vector.
Projecting a on b by mistake.

insider_note: The word VECTOR matters: divide by |a|² and keep the a, giving (4/3)(i − j − k). Dividing by |a| once instead gives the scalar projection, which answers a different question.
